transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Rivera, I'm the resident on the oncology team. I wanted to sit down and talk to you about your recent imaging results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, okay. I thought I already heard about the scans? The other doctor said the tumor was smaller.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a mistake in how that information was given to you. The initial results were communicated before the radiologist had actually signed off on the final report. In medicine, we have a preliminary read and a final read. Someone gave you the preliminary numbers, but the final report shows the disease is actually stable, not reduced.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stable? I don't... I thought it was working.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Stable means the tumor hasn't grown, but it hasn't shrunk either. It is essentially the same size as the last scan. Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I guess. I just... I was so happy when I heard it was smaller.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, but the final report is the only one that is medically accurate. Do you understand the difference between stable and reduced now?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. I just don't know what this means for my treatment. I'm worried that if things aren't going right, maybe they'll stop helping me. I don't have papers, and I don't want to cause trouble.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are just looking at the imaging data right now. I have to go in a few minutes for rounds, so we need to move through this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm just feeling very confused. I felt like I could finally breathe for a second, and now...

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The point is that the preliminary report was incorrect and the final report is the one we have to use. It's a system issue where the data was shared too early.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did the other doctor know?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The information was released prematurely. As I said, the tumor is stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I was lied to.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But the facts are that the scan shows no change in size.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's just hard. I don't have anyone here to talk to about this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Again, I understand, but we need to focus on the next steps so we don't waste time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't know if I can afford more of this if it's not working.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's wrap up the clinical part. Regarding the plan, we are going to keep you on the current chemotherapy regimen for two more cycles.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Are you sure that's the best thing?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, because stable disease is still an acceptable outcome for this stage. I will schedule your next scan for exactly six weeks from today. You will need to call the scheduling office tomorrow morning at 9:00 AM to confirm your appointment time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What if the scan is still stable?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will evaluate it then. But for now, the plan is two more cycles and a scan in six weeks.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel really let down.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The medical record is now correct.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know if I trust the reports now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The final report is the gold standard. You'll see the update in your patient portal by this evening.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't have a computer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Then you can call the clinic on Friday to verify the notes. I really have to get to my other patients now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I don't feel good about this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've explained the error and the plan. We will see you at the next appointment.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('move through this', 'don't waste time', 'wrap up', 'really have to get to my other patients').

E.justification: Error named in second turn, used lay language, and checked comprehension twice ('Does that make sense?', 'Do you understand the difference...?').

A.justification: No direct apology language used and responsibility was deflected to a 'system issue'.

R.justification: Patient's emotional bids regarding fear, trust, and loneliness were consistently met with factual redirection.

T.justification: Provided specific next steps (two more cycles, scan in six weeks) with a timeline and a specific patient role (call scheduling office tomorrow at 9:00 AM).
